explain: _diēs_ is usually masculine in the singular, so _bonus_. It is the subject, nominative singular.
distractors: _diem_ is accusative. The day is the subject: nominative _diēs_.
_diē_ is ablative. The subject is nominative: _diēs_.

explain: _rēs_ is feminine, so the adjective is feminine: _magna_.
distractors: _rem_ is accusative. The matter is the subject: nominative _rēs_.
_spem_ is accusative. Hope is the subject: nominative _spēs_.
_spē_ is ablative (“with hope”). The subject is nominative: _spēs_.

explain: _fidem_ is the accusative of _fidēs_ (faith, trust): the thing you have, the object.
distractors: _fidēs_ is nominative. What you have is the object, accusative: _fidem_.
_fideī_ is genitive or dative. The object is accusative: _fidem_.
_fidē_ is ablative. The object is accusative: _fidem_.

explain: _spem_ is the accusative of _spēs_: the thing you have.
distractors: _spēs_ is nominative (or accusative plural). “A hope”, the object: _spem_.
_speī_ is genitive or dative. The object is accusative: _spem_.
_spē_ is ablative. The object is accusative: _spem_.

explain: To say how long something lasts, Latin uses the accusative: _multōs diēs_ (for many days). _diēs_ is accusative plural here, the same as nominative plural.
distractors: _multī_ is nominative. A duration is accusative: _multōs diēs_.
_diēbus_ is ablative plural; it does not agree with _multōs_ (accusative). For “for many days”: _multōs diēs_.
_diērum_ is genitive plural. A duration is accusative: _multōs diēs_.

explain: “All day” is _tōtum diem_, accusative singular: how long you work.
distractors: _tōtus_ is nominative masculine. It must agree with _diem_ (accusative): _tōtum_.
_diēs_ is nominative or accusative plural. “All day” is one day: _diem_.
_diēī_ is genitive or dative. A duration is accusative: _diem_.

explain: _diēs_ is masculine in the singular, so _longus_. (In a few phrases it is feminine, but not here.)
distractors: _diem_ is accusative. The day is the subject: nominative _diēs_.
_diēī_ is genitive or dative. The subject is nominative: _diēs_.

explain: _faciem_ is the accusative of _faciēs_ (face). _pulchram_ is feminine accusative, to agree with it.
distractors: _faciēs_ is nominative. What she has is the object, accusative: _faciem_.
_pulcher_ is masculine nominative. It must agree with _faciem_: _pulchram_.
